text:
Mitch S: Heads up — we got paged twice in the last 2 hours for massive 429 spikes from a few customer tokens. CS is seeing queues for support escalations.
Emma L: Ugh, saw those alerts. Signals look like short-lived bursts, lots of token-level throttles firing, then recovering.
Zoe (CS): Customers reported degraded UX (time to first byte). Can we avoid paging CS for transient token bursts?
Rafael G: Agree. Current alert is org_quota_exhausted_total > 0 for 5m, which conflates per-org commits and per-key burst throttles. We should separate.
Priya C: Proposal: split alerts into two classes —
- Critical (page): sustained org-level quota exhaustion (>3m AND rate > X)
- Warning (no page): short-lived token or key-level 429 spikes, shown in dashboard and emailed to CS weekly.
Mitch S: Sounds right. Also need to debounce noisy rules and add grouping to reduce pager churn.
Emma L: For metrics, we have: token_429_count{org, key}, org_429_rate, token_bucket_replenish_rate. We can add a rolling-avg and burst-window.
Rafael G: Draft PromQL for the critical alert (sustained org-level):
```
(sum by (org) (rate(token_429_count[5m])) > 1) and (sum by (org) (rate(org_quota_exhausted_total[5m])) > 0)
```
This pages only when both 429s and quota exhaustion align.
Zoe (CS): Can the dashboard show the top 5 keys causing 429s per org so CS can reach out proactively?
Priya C: Yes. Panel idea: topk(5, sum by (key, org) (rate(token_429_count[10m]))) with links to the keys table.
Mitch S: Also add a metric for "burst_return_to_baseline_seconds" to suppress paging for bursts that auto-resolve within X seconds.
Emma L: For runbook actions in the page:
1) Check org-level quota metrics on the org panel.
2) If org quota exhausted, escalate to Billing/CS.
3) If only one token spiking, check client SDK version + recent deploys, adjust per-key limits if necessary.
Rafael G: We need to change alert annotations to include suggested next steps and quick links (grafana panels, list keys, ticket template). Example annotation:
"runbook_url: https://confluence.redwood/sre/runbooks/rate-limits"
Priya C: Operationally, let's set page thresholds: page if org_429_rate > 0.5 req/s sustained for 10m OR org_quota_exhausted_total increase > 0. Page suppressed if burst_return_to_baseline_seconds < 300.
Zoe (CS): For customer comms, we prefer being notified via a digest for warnings. Only page for real outages.
OncallBot: Incident created: INC-2026 | Trigger: org_429_rate_high | Assigned: @Mitch S | Link: https://incidents.redwood/INC-2026
Mitch S: Assigned, I'll do triage and update this thread with findings.
Emma L: Action items:
- Rafael: update Prometheus rules + annot.
- Priya: add burst_return metric and hook into alert logic.
- Mitch: create dashboard panel for top keys + add link in alert.
- Zoe: prepare CS digest template and criteria.
Rafael G: I'll put a PR for the rules (prometheus/rules/alerts_rate_limits.yml) and include the new annotations.
Priya C: I'll instrument burst_return_to_baseline_seconds. Proposed label: latency_class and org.
Zoe (CS): Thx team — if this reduces pager noise, CS can focus on real escalations.
Mitch S: Closing loop — will post follow-up once PRs merge and we run load tests.
OncallBot: Alert resolved: org_429_rate_high (1772504688) — auto-resolved after metric fell below threshold.
Mitch S: Resolved for now, keeping open until dashboards and rules are live.
